newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon sees HK GDP growth above 5 pct achievable.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees HK GDP growth above 5 pct achievable.

text.p: Economic growth of more than five percent is achievable in Hong Kong this year despite the the government's decision to revise down its forecast to 4.7 percent, Salomon Brothers said on Thursday.

Growth in gross domestic product (GDP) in excess of five percent, possibly as high as 5.2 percent, was attainable given a number of encouraging trends in consumer expenditure and external trade, said Kevin Chan, Salomon regional economist.

"One of the major factors contributing to our expectation for a continued improvement in the GDP growth rate is the recovery in retail sales during the first half of the year," Chan said in a statement.

"Retail sales growth indicates a rise in total consumer expenditure, which accounts for 60 percent of GDP. Although the recovery is still modest, retail sales growth has now broken through the negative growth period of 1995, which registered a 1.4 percent shrinkage."

Salomon in August forecast GDP to grow by 5.2 percent this year, but the Hong Kong government revised down its GDP forecast in September to 4.7 percent from five percent, blaming the shift on weaker than expected trade in the first six months.
Some analysts have said the government's revised outlook was still over-optimistic and even 4.7 percent may be hard to reach.
But Chan said he remained unswayed.

"As inflationary pressure now appears quite subdued, thanks to lower increases in food prices and rents, we have also revised our forecast for the average inflation rate for 1996 down to seven percent from eight percent," he added.
